Swift enum descriptor 0x330c declares 11 payload and 13 empty cases; field descriptor 0x3710 agrees. Outer enum descriptor 0x3328 and its ABI-declared cached singleton accessor 0x17e4 establish the metadata passed to the exact libswiftCore runtime tag call at 0x14b4. Every incoming path to the outlined getter is dominated by that call and selects outer tag 0; reflection field 0x3850 directly references fixed enum descriptor 0x330c. Its static enum metadata 0x4330 points back to that descriptor and declares value-witness table 0x42b0, value size 156 and complete straight-line getEnumTag function 0x23fc. On every path the unchanged incoming outer object is copied at offset zero by the exact libSystem memcpy import into a fixed private frame interval of that size; no intervening unknown call or overlapping write is admitted. The getter called at 0x1538 targets 0x1844, either that declared getter or an equal complete straight-line body, and reads only that interval. Shared helper code never supplies enum identity or count. Its unchanged tag reaches the LDRSW index after an explicit 32-bit zero-extending write. Signed 32-bit entries at 0x1784 are added to 0x1554. REA+ restored computed edges, disassembled destinations and extended the owning function before observations; generated override labels are analysis metadata, not source/caller declarations. Under trusted-darwin-arm64-chkstk-v1, normal-return call at 0x14a8 binds exact ___chkstk_darwin from /usr/lib/libSystem.B.dylib (external 0x30, import slot 0x4010). X2/X8/X12/SP retain reaching values; other volatile registers, including X9/X10/X16/X17/X30, and flags remain unknown. The probe may read stack/thread state and fault; its 16-byte scratch write is [-288,-272) relative to function-entry SP, disjoint from admitted live private storage. No allocation or exact runtime binding is inferred. On supported non-Windows AArch64 Mach-O inputs, REA+ can restore signed-word Swift enum dispatches from verified ABI metadata, accessor and instruction flow. Generated switch overrides are analysis metadata. Recovery budgets are 4096 cases, 100000 CFG/reaching-definition work units per candidate function and 256 nested queries; unsupported or exhausted paths remain unrecovered, not complete.

The default profile requires Ghidra to report default auto-analysis complete; an explicitly bounded profile can admit a stable partial Program after its configured deadline. Every observation reports the measured analysis outcome.
The imported Program and temporary project are ephemeral and deleted on close. Annotation operations edit session database metadata; original executable bytes are never written.
Cancelling an active Ghidra request terminates its ephemeral database and discards session annotations. The selected target remains open; the next provider query imports the original artifact again.
Default-space addresses use lowercase 0x-prefixed hexadecimal; other address spaces use <percent-encoded-space>:0x<hex>.
References cover the complete Ghidra function-body AddressSet and exact entry. Dossier incoming edges omit sources owned by that function; procedure_references also retains those internal edges.
The dossier combines Ghidra FunctionManager, Listing, ReferenceManager, BasicBlockModel, and decompiler observations; provider-specific pseudocode and assembly are not cross-provider text invariants.

Resolved reference metadata identifies computed, indirect, external, call, jump, and data edges; unresolved targetless flows remain unknown, and function classifications distinguish thunks and externals.
Synthetic Ghidra entry-point references without actionable memory sources are omitted.
The Java bridge serializes one function request per Program and lets each decompilation run until it completes or the caller cancels.
